title: Barbara Kruger
description: Books, catalogues, magazine covers, multiples and ephemera by Barbara Kruger, from the 1983 ICA London catalogue to the 2024 Serpentine mirror.
intro: Barbara Kruger (b. 1945, Newark, New Jersey) worked through the late 1960s and 1970s as a designer and picture editor at Condé Nast, much of it at Mademoiselle. From the late 1970s she used that training against the magazine page: found black-and-white photographs, cropped hard, with short lines set in Futura Bold Oblique, white on a red bar. Lines like Your body is a battleground and We won't play nature to your culture address the viewer directly and leave open who is speaking, on power, money, gender and the act of looking.

Her first institutional solo show opened at the ICA, London, in 1983 and travelled to the Kunsthalle Basel. The Museum of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles, gave her a retrospective in 1999, shown at the Whitney in 2000, and she received the Golden Lion for lifetime achievement at the 2005 Venice Biennale. From the 1990s the work grew to cover whole buildings, floors, walls and escalators, and in Siena in 2002 thirteen city buses. Thinking of You. I Mean Me. I Mean You. opened at the Art Institute of Chicago in 2021 and went on to LACMA, MoMA and the Serpentine in London.

The collection holds her catalogues from the 1983 ICA book on, Remote Control, her collected writing on television, film and power, the two New York covers she made in 2016 and 2022, a 1983 transit placard, two multiples, and postcards, an exhibition invitation and a bandana.
